# CISAC - Center for International Security and Cooperation

> > Stanford's Center for International Security and Cooperation (CISAC) conducts research and hosts seminars on nuclear security, nonproliferation, defense technology, terrorism, and global security challenges.

CISAC is a research center within Stanford's Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies (FSI) that brings together scholars, policymakers, and experts to address critical international security issues including nuclear weapons policy, arms control, civil-military relations, and emerging security threats.

## Key Topics

- Nuclear nonproliferation
- National security policy
- U.S.-India nuclear deal
- UN weapons inspections (UNSCOM/UNMOVIC)
- Civil-military relations
- Homeland security
- Counterterrorism
- Defense technology and RMA
- Nuclear weapons programs
- Uranium supply and plutonium production
- Missile defense
- Democratic peace theory
- Chinese economic reform
- Presidential powers and national security law

## Nuclear Security and Nonproliferation

- [India's Uranium Supply and Plutonium Production Capability](http://cisac.fsi.stanford.edu/events/indias_uranium_supply_and_plutonium_production_capability): CISAC seminar on India's nuclear program and U.S.-India deal by Chaim Braun
- [From UNSCOM to the UN Monitoring, Verification and Inspection Commission (UNMOVIC)](http://cisac.fsi.stanford.edu/events/from_unscom_to_the_un_monitoring_verification_and_inspection_commission_unmovic): Seminar on UN weapons inspections transition with Terry Taylor
- [Evidence of Academic Fraud and Possible Criminality in Federally Funded National Missile Defense Research at MIT](http://cisac.fsi.stanford.edu/events/evidence_of_academic_fraud_and_possible_criminality_in_federally_funded_national_missile_defense_research_at_mit): CISAC seminar on research misconduct in MIT missile defense program

## Defense and Security Policy

- [Politics and Technology: The Civil Dimension of the Revolution in Military Affairs](http://cisac.fsi.stanford.edu/events/politics_and_technology_the_civil_dimension_of_the_revolution_in_military_affairs): Karen Guttieri on civil-military aspects of defense technology
- [A Different Kind of War Makes a Different Kind of State: Organizing for Homeland Security](http://cisac.fsi.stanford.edu/events/a_different_kind_of_war_makes_a_different_kind_of_state_organizing_for_homeland_security): Paul Stockton discusses homeland security organization and policy
- [The Court's Attack on the Presidency: National Security and the Separation of Powers vs. Prosecutorial Zeal and Judicial Myopia](http://cisac.fsi.stanford.edu/events/the_courts_attack_on_the_presidency_national_security_and_the_separation_of_powers_vs_prosecutorial_zeal_and_judicial_myopia): Herbert Abrams on presidential powers and national security law

## Terrorism and Conflict Studies

- [Tactical Prevention of Suicide Bombings in Israel](http://cisac.fsi.stanford.edu/events/tactical_prevention_of_suicide_bombings_in_israel): Edward Kaplan presents counterterrorism operations research for Israel
- [Political Violence, Democratization, and Peace Accords: Testing the 'Democratic Peace' Thesis in Latin America](http://cisac.fsi.stanford.edu/events/political_violence_democratization_and_peace_accords_testing_the_democratic_peace_thesis_in_latin_america): Carlo Nasi examines democratic peace theory in Latin American conflicts

## Global Political Economy

- [Bird in a Cage: What do we know about Chinese Economic Reform?](http://cisac.fsi.stanford.edu/events/bird_in_a_cage_what_do_we_know_about_chinese_economic_reform): Chi Zhang discusses Chinese economic reform at CISAC event
